contents.name: §62 (62.8)-(62.10): the retarded potentials, the retarded-time prescription and the additive homogeneous solution

contents.name: §63 (63.1) with the footnote's light-cone argument: for each t the equation t'+R(t')/c=t has just one root t' when the particle velocity is everywhere less than c
contents.support: Clause (a) is the event-form library version: the light-cone intersection argument is replaced by strict decrease of s->t-s-|x-z(s)|/c plus the intermediate value theorem, with the uniform bound |z'|<=v_*<c as an explicit hypothesis.

contents.name: §63 (63.6)-(63.7): the implicit derivatives dt'/dt and grad t'
contents.support: Clause (a): the two derivative formulas are d_t s=kappa^{-1} and grad_x s=-n/(c kappa) in the design's normalization (kappa=1-n.beta).

contents.name: §63 (63.8)-(63.9): the electric field split into a velocity part decaying like 1/R^2 and an acceleration part decaying like 1/R, and H=(R/R) x E in LL units
contents.support: Clauses (c)-(d): E=E_vel+E_acc and B=n x E/c with C=q/(4 pi eps_0); the library adds the explicit uniform remainder bound on the velocity part.

contents.name: §66 (66.3)-(66.6): fields at large distances inversely proportional to the first power of R, the combination t-R'/c, and the R^2 energy-flux argument
contents.support: Clause (d): source backing for the 1/r acceleration term dominating the remainder along the ray family; the explicit uniform constant is proved locally from the displayed formulas.

contents.name: §38 printed pp. 91-93: the field of a uniformly moving charge (Heaviside ellipsoid) referenced by the constant-velocity specialization of (63.8)
contents.reason: The uniformly moving charge specialization is not consumed by this pair's items; its physical statements belong to the later physics pages (postulates of the field, retarded potentials and radiation).

contents.name: §64-§65 printed pp. 163-165 (spectral resolution of the retarded potentials; second-order Lagrangian) and §67-§80 (radiation of charges)
contents.reason: Fourier spectral resolution, the second-order Lagrangian and single-charge radiation power are scheduled on later mathematics and physics pages (radiation asymptotics, action formulation); this pair stops at the field formulas and the far-zone remainder.

contents.name: §10.3.1 pp. 429-430: 'at most one point on the trajectory is in communication' - two retarded points would force an average velocity c

contents.name: §10.3.1 (10.37)-(10.38) with the moving-train discussion: the retardation factor (1-n.v/c)^{-1} for integrals of the density evaluated at retarded times
contents.support: Clauses (a)-(b): this factor is kappa=1-n.beta, the emission-time Jacobian and the exact weight (kappa r)^{-1} of the pairing identity.

contents.name: §10.3.1 (10.39)-(10.40): the Liénard-Wiechert potentials V and A
contents.support: Clause (b): phi=C/(kappa r) and A=beta phi/c with C=q/(4 pi eps_0); the derivation is consumed from lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields and only restated here.

contents.name: §10.3.2 (10.65)-(10.66): the field of a point charge in arbitrary motion, in the u=c n-v form, and B=(1/c) n x E
contents.support: Clause (c): equivalent to the displayed E_vel+E_acc after substituting (n.u)=c kappa; the library keeps the invariant n, beta, kappa normalization.

contents.name: §10.3.2 p. 438: the first term is the 'generalized Coulomb field (velocity field)' falling off as 1/r^2, the second the 'radiation field (acceleration field)' falling off as 1/r and dominant at large distances
contents.support: Clauses (c)-(d): terminology, rates and the far-zone dominance; the explicit uniform constant C(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3} is proved locally and is stronger than the source's asymptotic remark.

contents.name: §10.1-§10.1.3 printed pp. 416-422: gauge transformations, Coulomb and Lorenz gauges, and the wave equations for the potentials

canonical.name: The theorem's own assembly: event-form retarded root with the emission-time Jacobian, the delta-substitution pairing identity with weight (kappa r)^{-1}, the velocity/acceleration split with the uniform velocity-field bound, and the uniform far-zone remainder with its explicit constant
canonical.support: Locally assembled from the cited treatments: root and Jacobian from the strict-decrease/intermediate-value/implicit-function argument (LL (63.1), (63.6)-(63.7); Griffiths (10.33); Tong (6.36)); delta substitution from Tong (6.33)-(6.34) and Griffiths (10.37)-(10.38); fields from LL (63.8)-(63.9), Griffiths (10.65)-(10.66) and Tong (6.42), (6.44)-(6.45); the uniform remainder bound is the library's own explicit estimate on the displayed velocity term (ai-altered sharpening of the sources' 1/R^2 versus 1/R asymptotic remarks).
